title: GCP Marketplace procurement steps (internal cheatsheet)
content:
Purpose
- Help AEs/SEs/CS/Support move a buyer from “we need to buy via GCP Marketplace” → active subscription/offer accepted → Redwood org provisioned → first successful API call → billing dimensions verified.
- This is NOT customer-facing. Use customer FAQ / docs for external language.

When to use this
- Customer mandates procurement via GCP Marketplace (common for: enterprise security + centralized billing + spend commitments).
- Customer asks for Private Offer (discounted pricing, committed spend, or custom terms).
- Customer wants Marketplace “paper trail” even if they will use Dedicated/Private deployment.

Quick triage (ask these 6 questions first)
1) Is the customer buying from GCP Marketplace (self-serve public listing) OR via a Private Offer?
2) Which Redwood product surface: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private (VPC/on-prem), and/or compliance add-ons?
3) Which GCP billing account will be charged? (ID + owner team)
4) Who at the customer has permissions to:
   - accept Marketplace agreements
   - select the billing account
   - create/approve procurement orders (if required internally)
5) Do they already have a Redwood org? If yes, what is the org slug + admin email?
6) Any constraints: data residency, KMS, audit logs, retention, VPC-SC, IP allowlisting, SSO?

Typical GCP Marketplace procurement flow (public listing)
0) Pre-check (Redwood side)
- Confirm correct SKU(s) and expected billing dimensions for the customer use case.
- Confirm whether customer needs Dedicated/Private: marketplace “purchase” may cover billing + entitlement, but deployment/provisioning steps differ.
- If regulated: send security packet links + confirm what’s public vs on-request.

1) Customer subscribes in Cloud Marketplace
- Customer navigates to: GCP Console → Marketplace → Redwood Inference listing.
- Click “Subscribe” / “Purchase” (language varies by listing type).
- Customer selects:
  - Billing account (this is the #1 place procurement gets stuck)
  - Project / organization context (varies; often they must be in the right Cloud Org)
- Customer accepts terms.

2) Entitlement created (GCP → Redwood)
- After subscription, GCP creates an entitlement.
- Redwood entitlement sync job pulls entitlement and associates it to a Redwood org (new or existing).
- Expected timing: usually minutes; can be longer during propagation delays.

3) Customer provisions/links Redwood org
- Customer goes to Redwood Console → “Marketplace onboarding” entrypoint.
- They either:
  - Create a new Redwood org, OR
  - Link subscription to an existing org (common for pilots that started direct)
- Console validates entitlement and shows next steps.

4) Customer creates first API key + runs first request
- Ensure they:
  - create API key
  - confirm model access / quotas
  - run a simple test (curl or SDK) to generate the first successful request

5) Billing verification (GCP Billing + Redwood metering)
- GCP billing line items may lag (often not instant).
- Redwood internal usage should appear immediately; marketplace billing may show after processing.
- If customer reports mismatch, follow “Billing blockers” below.

Private Offer flow (most enterprise deals)
A) Redwood drafts Private Offer (Commercial + Legal)
- AE/Partnerships requests private offer approval per discount guardrails.
- Confirm:
  - Offer start/end date
  - Committed spend or rate card
  - Included SKUs/dimensions
  - Support/SLA terms alignment

B) Customer accepts Private Offer in GCP Marketplace
- Customer must accept with the correct billing account and org.
- Common failure: customer accepts in wrong Cloud Organization or wrong billing account.

C) Entitlement + provisioning
- Same as public listing after acceptance, but entitlement may not appear until offer is active.

Customer permissions checklist (common source of delays)
- Ask customer to involve an admin who can do both Marketplace + Billing.

Recommended minimum (customer-side)
- Billing Account Administrator (to attach charges to billing account)
- Marketplace Admin / Procurement role (to subscribe/accept offers)
- Project IAM rights sufficient to view marketplace subscription context

Common note
- Many customers split responsibilities: procurement can accept terms but cannot pick a billing account; cloud platform team can pick billing account but is not involved in vendor procurement. Make sure both are on the thread.

Common blockers + how to unblock

1) “Subscribe” button greyed out / can’t accept offer
Symptoms
- Customer says they can view listing but cannot subscribe or accept offer.
Likely causes
- Missing Marketplace permissions
- Not in correct Cloud Organization / wrong account
What to do
- Ask for screenshot + exact error text.
- Ask who is signed in and what Cloud Org they’re in.
- Suggest they try from an admin account with Billing + Marketplace permissions.
Escalate
- If the error looks like a GCP-side policy enforcement: route to Partnerships for partner escalation.

2) Billing account selection issues
Symptoms
- Customer can subscribe but cannot select the intended billing account.
Likely causes
- They don’t have billing admin permissions
- Billing account is closed/locked, or policy-restricted
What to do
- Get billing account ID.
- Confirm they have Billing Account Administrator.
- If they must use a specific billing account for compliance, ensure procurement uses that account at acceptance time.
Escalate
- Partnerships + AE to align customer’s cloud platform owner.

3) Entitlement not found in Redwood Console
Symptoms
- Customer subscribed/accepted offer but Redwood Console says “No active marketplace entitlement found” or similar.
Likely causes
- Entitlement propagation delay
- Customer subscribed under different email / different cloud org context than expected
- Entitlement sync job delays
What to do (in order)
- Confirm purchase timestamp + billing account + (if available) entitlement ID.
- Ask customer to wait 10–20 minutes and retry.
- If still failing, ask them to confirm they accepted the right offer (public vs private offer) and not a draft.
- Internally: check entitlement verification endpoint / logs.
Escalate
- #eng-platform for entitlement sync health
- Chloe Martin (Console onboarding) for UX/error code mapping
- Ethan Park (control plane) if entitlement verification endpoint looks wrong

4) Customer already has a Redwood org and wants to “merge” or link
Symptoms
- Existing org from direct signup; procurement wants marketplace billing.
What to do
- Use “link subscription to existing org” path.
- Confirm org slug + current org admin email.
- Confirm there are no competing subscriptions already linked.
Escalate
- ENG-22115 (multi-subscription edge cases) if console blocks linking unexpectedly.

5) Billing dimension mismatch / unexpected line items
Symptoms
- Customer sees billing dimension names that don’t match what we promised, or rates look wrong.
Likely causes
- Incorrect SKU→dimension mapping
- Customer on legacy listing/SKU
- Private offer includes wrong dimension set
What to do
- Capture:
  - GCP billing export line item (dimension name + timestamp)
  - Redwood invoice/usage export snippet (internal meter)
  - Subscription/offer identifier
- Validate against current SKU catalog mapping.
Escalate
- Cole Summers (billing/metering) + Nadia Rahman (telemetry)
- Reference known issue pattern: “dimension mismatch found” (check recent incidents/tickets)

6) Security questionnaire / “we need SOC2 / encryption / audit logs before subscribing”
What to do
- Share the marketplace security documentation pack index.
- Offer to do a 30-min security review call (SE + Security as needed).
- Be precise: don’t over-claim on certifications or data deletion timelines.
Escalate
- Naomi Feldman (security/compliance product owner)
- Olga Petrov (GRC evidence)
- Marcus Lin (security engineering)

Expected timelines (set expectations)
- Public listing subscription → entitlement available: typically minutes; can be up to ~1 hour in edge cases.
- Private offer acceptance → entitlement available: often minutes after effective time; can be delayed if offer start date is future.
- Billing line items in GCP console: not real-time; can lag.

Who to contact internally (escalation matrix)

Primary aliases (use these first)
- marketplace@redwoodinference.com (Partnerships triage)
- support@redwoodinference.com (customer-facing support queue)
- security@redwoodinference.com (security packet / evidence requests)
- billing@redwoodinference.com (billing/metering questions)

Slack channels (internal)
- #partnerships (marketplace / partner escalation)
- #deal-desk (private offer approvals, discount guardrails)
- #eng-platform (entitlement sync / control plane)
- #eng-billing (metering, dimensions)
- #support-escalations (customer-impacting delays)

Named contacts (when you need a person)
- Partnerships / Marketplace motions: Stephanie Nguyen
- EMEA-specific procurement nuances: Lukas Meyer
- Deal ops / CRM workflow for marketplace deals: Isabelle Laurent
- Billing/metering mapping + dimension issues: Cole Summers
- Telemetry/usage reporting: Nadia Rahman
- Console onboarding flow + error states: Chloe Martin
- Control plane / entitlement verification: Ethan Park
- Security packet + questionnaire owner: Naomi Feldman
- Evidence / SOC2 artifact access: Olga Petrov
- Security engineering deep dives (encryption/KMS/audit): Marcus Lin
- Support escalation owner (if customer blocked >24h): Dev Patel
- Commercial counsel (terms wording / offer language): Sofia Mendes
- Finance (pricing guardrails / credits/refunds): Laura Bennett

Standard internal “next steps” checklist (copy/paste into deal thread)
- [ ] Confirm: public listing vs private offer
- [ ] Confirm: billing account ID + owner
- [ ] Confirm: customer has Billing Account Admin + Marketplace acceptance permissions
- [ ] Confirm: Redwood org exists? (slug + admin email)
- [ ] Provide: marketplace onboarding link + expected entitlement timing
- [ ] Instrument: ask customer to share exact timestamp of subscribe/accept + screenshot of any error
- [ ] If no entitlement after 20 min: escalate to #eng-platform with timestamp + customer domain + billing account ID

Email/snippet: what we tell the customer when entitlement is delayed (approved tone)
“Thanks — we see occasional propagation delays between GCP Marketplace subscription and vendor entitlement activation. In most cases the entitlement is available within a few minutes, but it can take a bit longer depending on GCP processing. If you can share the timestamp you subscribed/accepted the offer and the billing account used, we can verify the entitlement on our side and help you get unblocked.”

Notes / gotchas (things that repeatedly bite us)
- Customer accepts the offer under the wrong billing account and later asks us to “move it.” We generally can’t; they may need to re-subscribe/accept correctly.
- Private offer start date set in the future → customer expects immediate activation.
- Customer has multiple Cloud Orgs; procurement signs in with a different identity than the one their cloud platform team uses.
- Existing Redwood org with active direct billing: linking marketplace changes billing source; ensure CS/AE aligns expectations.
- If customer is strict on residency/retention: get Security involved early; do not ad-lib.

Changelog
- 2026-02-18: Added entitlement delay language + updated escalation matrix (Dev Patel / Chloe Martin) and clarified billing line item lag expectations.
- 2026-01-28: Initial version compiled from GCP partner review + internal onboarding dry runs.
